text: Neutron stars matter here, because they make an enormous cosmological story risk being wrong. Their masses can be measured through pulsar timing. In the chain examined here, ideas about particle physics and ultra-dense matter lead to a proposed neutron star mass ceiling, which is then tied to cosmological natural selection. The authors named two observations that could break that chain, a sufficiently heavy neutron star, or a well-measured pair of neutron stars whose masses differ by more than 4%. Either test was meant to count.
